  • - While kneading the dough, the melted butter and the salt should not touch directly the leavening, as this would retard fermentation. Therefore mix the salt with the flour and add the butter in the end when all ingredients are already mixed with the leavening.

  • • \frac{1}{2} cups flour
  • • \frac{1}{2} cup sugar
  • • 8 oz. ground almonds
  • • 3 sticks butter
  • • 2 packages vanilla sugar (1 package into dough, 1 for sprinkling)
  • • 4 tablespoons sugar mixed with vanilla sugar

children.block_description: A paragraph or line of text.
children.html: On a floured pastry board knead all ingredients into a ball. Use palms of your hands, not fingers, so that dough will not crumble. Dough is ready when smooth and no longer sticks to the board. Refrigerate 1 hour, or overnight as it will be easier to work with. Shape tiny horns the size of your little finger or smaller, according to your preference and patience. A small grinder is available in some speciality stores, which makes them all equal in size and is faster than the "manual method". Place horns on a clean dry cookie sheet, 1" apart. Preheat oven to 325F, bake 15-20 minutes, until pale golden. Remove from oven and let stand 5 minutes. While hot, sprinkle with sugar mixed with vanilla sugar. When cooled remove carefully from cookie sheet. They keep for many weeks in an airtight tin.

• • 2 cups flour
  • • 1/3 cup sugar mixed with 1 teaspoon vanilla sugar
  • • 1 stick butter
  • • 2 tablespoons milk
  • • grated rind of 1 lemon
  • • red raspberry or red currant preserve

children.block_description: A paragraph or line of text.
children.html: On a floured pastry board knead all ingredients into a ball using the palms of your hands, not the fingers. The dough will be smooth and will not crumble. You can let it rest for a few hours, overnight or more. You can use it right away also.

children.block_description: A paragraph or line of text.
children.html: With a roller pin roll the dough out as thin as possible. (1/8"). Cut it into 1-1/4" round cakes, using a cookie cutter or a glass. Separate half of the round cakes and cut out a small round hole in the center, the size of a thimble. Use a cookie cutter or a thimble. Place the round cakes on a clean, dry cookie sheet and bake at 350F for 15 minutes, or until they are pink/golden. Remove from oven and cool. Before serving put 1/2 teaspoon of red raspberry or red currant seedless preserve in the center of each plain round, top it with one "holed" round. The red color is important for the look of the cookies and the sour flavor of raspberry or currant compliments them well. Unfilled cookies can be stored for weeks in an airtight container.

children.html: Pour the cream in a saucepan and set over medium heat. When hot, but not boiling, add sugar, vanilla sugar and the ground nuts. Stirring steadily, boil until the mixture stiffens and separates from the pan. Remove from heat. Let it cool or refrigerate overnight. Next day: Make little balls, dip each in egg white and dredge in grated chocolate. Let the "truffles" dry for 10 minutes and place them in petit-four holders.
